cf.title: Fix XLogFileReadAnyTLI silently applying divergent WAL from wrong timeline

input.subject: Fix XLogFileReadAnyTLI silently applying divergent WAL from wrong timeline

verdict_reasoning: The problem is stated and the demand is shown: a production switchover in message #1, an earlier report in message #2, and a reproduction back to v12 in message #5. One fixable level 2 objection survived, replication-ondisk-1: the back-patched wait is explained only at DEBUG1 and no text tells operators what to do when the segment never arrives. A committer who knows recovery must sign for a behaviour change in back branches.

brief.title: Stop archive recovery from reading divergent WAL from a parent timeline
brief.problem: When the switch-point segment of the target timeline is not yet archived, XLogFileReadAnyTLI() falls back to the parent timeline's segment with the same number. That copy holds WAL from the old primary after the switch, so a standby replays divergent data without an error and can no longer reach the target timeline. The author hit this during a planned HA switchover.
brief.proposed_design: After it skips timelines that began in a later segment, XLogFileReadAnyTLI() tries only the newest eligible timeline for the segment. If that file is in neither the archive nor pg_wal, recovery waits for it and does not read a parent-timeline copy. This replaces the old targetBeginSeg check, which guarded only the target timeline's own switch point and missed intermediate timelines.
user_visible_surface: Archive recovery now waits for the switch-point segment of the owning timeline where it used to replay the parent timeline's copy.
New DEBUG1 message "not searching older timelines for WAL segment" when recovery declines to fall back.
author_claims: Fixes silent replay of divergent WAL, including a three-timeline case the old guard missed.
A visible stall is better than silently applying divergent data, even for setups that rely on the fallback.
Ants Aasma's earlier patch from a linked thread is functionally equivalent.
A reviewer reports the bug reproduces back to v12; the commit message targets back-patch through 14.
Two new TAP tests cover the two- and three-timeline cases and check that recovery finishes once the correct segment appears.
brief.thread_state: Surya Poondla and solai v reviewed v4 and call it ready for a committer; Surya still asks that the DEBUG1 message fire only when an older timeline exists. The separate walreceiver state patch (0002/0003) was disputed by Stepan Tyagushev and dropped from v4, to move to its own thread.
unclear: The material does not say why the earlier 2022 thread with the equivalent patch did not end in a commit.
The patch does not handle a child timeline that dies before archiving its switch-point segment; recovery then waits forever, and no stop at the exact switch LSN is offered.
The patch has no documentation or release-note text for the behaviour change in back branches.
The author does not say whether the DEBUG1 message will be limited to cases with an older timeline.

objections.title: Back-patched stall can leave existing standbys waiting with no visible log message
objections.failure_scenario: A standby on v14-v18 takes a minor update. Later a cascading failover promotes a child timeline that dies before archiving its switch-point segment. Before the update, recovery replayed the parent copy and went on; after it, recovery waits forever, and the only sign at default log levels is that recovery stops moving.
objections.argument: Message #5 names this case and accepts the stall as the right default, but asks that it be stated. The v4 commit message does not mention it, and the patch adds no docs or release-note text. Message #10 keeps the only explanation at DEBUG1 and sends it on every retry, including on single-timeline standbys (message #11). In a minor release, a committer would likely want users to be able to tell this new wait from a hang, and to know what to do about it.
objections.author_must_show: How does an operator on a back branch learn that recovery is waiting for the owning timeline's switch-point segment, and what are they told to do when that segment will never be archived?

critic.reasoning: Message #5 accepts the stall but asks that the commit message state the case, and v4 does not. Message #10 keeps the only explanation at DEBUG1, and no text tells back-branch operators what to do when the segment never arrives.

refuted.title: Back-patched recovery stall has no visible signal or escape path
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator applies a minor release on 14 or later to a standby whose child timeline archived its history file but died before archiving the switch-point segment. Recovery used to continue from the parent copy and now waits forever. At the default log level only repeated restore_command attempts appear, so the operator sees a hang and has no setting to get past it.
refuted.argument: The commit message targets back-patch through 14, so the stall reaches existing standbys in a minor release without anyone asking for it. Message #5 names this cascading-failover case, and the brief records that the patch offers no stop at the switch LSN. The new message "not searching older timelines for WAL segment" stays at DEBUG1 (message #10), so a stall that the author defends as better because it is visible is in fact silent at normal log levels. The v4 commit message does not describe this case, and the patch adds no release-note or documentation text for operators.
refuted.author_must_show: How does an operator on a back branch learn that recovery is waiting for the owning timeline's segment, and what can they do when that segment no longer exists?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1. This version also says the operator has no setting to get past the stall, which the material does not establish.

refuted.title: Back-patched stall is visible only at DEBUG1 and has no documented way out
refuted.failure_scenario: After a minor update, a cascading failover leaves a child timeline whose history file is archived but whose switch-point segment never is. The standby used to continue and now waits forever. At the default log level it prints nothing beyond the retries, so the operator finds out only from replication lag and has no documented recovery step.
refuted.argument: Message #5 names this case and accepts the stall, and the brief records that no stop at the exact switch LSN is offered. Message #10 keeps the only new diagnostic at DEBUG1 for the tests, so production logs do not say why recovery stopped. The commit message targets back-patch through 14 but includes no documentation or release-note text. A committer would likely ask what operators of back branches should do when this happens, for example set recovery_target_timeline to the parent timeline.
refuted.author_must_show: How will an operator on a minor release see that recovery is waiting for a switch-point segment, and what documented step lets them recover?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which states the same back-branch stall and missing operator guidance and also covers the DEBUG1 message firing on single-timeline standbys.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The patch changes which WAL segment file archive recovery reads at a timeline switch point in xlogrecovery.c.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The v4 commit message targets back-patch through 14, and recovery then waits where it used to continue.

questions: How does an operator on a back branch learn, at the default log level, that recovery is waiting for the owning timeline's switch-point segment?
What should an operator do when the child timeline died before archiving its switch-point segment, so the segment will never arrive?
Will the commit message and release notes state the cascading-failover case from message #5, where recovery now waits and used to continue?
Will the DEBUG1 message "not searching older timelines for WAL segment" fire only when an older timeline exists, as the reviewer asks?
Why did the 2022 thread with the functionally equivalent patch end without a commit, and does that reason apply here?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows archive recovery and timeline switching in xlogrecovery.c, and who is willing to back-patch a behaviour change. No committer has spoken in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a recovery behaviour change in every supported branch from 14 on. Any standby that waits after a minor update where it used to continue becomes the committer's report to answer, for the life of those branches.
committability.author_follow_up: The author produced four versions, dropped the disputed walreceiver patches from v4, and plans separate threads for two related issues.

priority.reason: The bug causes silent replay of divergent WAL for standbys that use a WAL archive across a timeline switch, and two reviewers call v4 ready for a committer. The patch is about 14 KiB in one recovery file plus tests, but no committer is engaged and back-patching needs care.

provisional_note: The code was not read. Whether the new rule is correct when several switch points fall in one segment, or when the segment exists only in pg_wal, could not be judged.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Archive current timeline history file on archiver startup if needed
precedents_retrieved.summary: When a primary on a timeline above 1 has WAL archiving enabled after its last timeline switch, the history file for its current timeline is never archived. This breaks cascading standbys and explicit-timeline PITR built from `-X none` base backups. The patch proposed archiving that history file if it is not yet archived, first at archiver startup and later at the end of StartupXLOG, with an alternative patch letting recovery proceed when the initial timeline's history file cannot be fetched.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Kyotaro Horiguchi objected to archiving the same file repeatedly. Robert Haas rejected the alternative of fetching the history file and ignoring errors, and asked whether the two patches were alternatives. After Robert Haas's review the author did not reply, the entry was set to Waiting on Author, and it was later returned with feedback because the feedback had not been addressed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It seems to me that trying to fetch a timeline history file and then
ignoring any error has got to be wrong.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add timeline to partial WAL segments
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the timeline that a promoted server switches to into the name of the .partial WAL segment it archives, for example 000000010000000100000001.00000002.partial. This prevents archive conflicts when several promotions in HA setups produce the same .partial file; prioritizing .history files in the archiver was proposed alongside it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped working on it. After discussion, Michael Paquier agreed with a revised scheme in which pg_receivewal would also use the timeline-suffixed name. The author then marked the patch Waiting on Author because it needed more work, and no new version followed for about 20 months. Robert Haas and Michael Paquier also objected to back-patching the naming change into minor releases, but that did not decide the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: As nothing has happened here, I have marked the patch as RwF.

precedents_retrieved.title: get current and recovery timeline
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set out to let tools read the current timeline of a standby from shared memory, first by allowing pg_walfile_name() on a standby and later through new functions that return the LSN and timeline together. The last version changed pg_stat_get_wal_receiver() to return the last known values when no WAL receiver runs, and added applied_lsn and applied_tli columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected to the last version because pg_stat_wal_receiver maps one to one to the shared memory state of a running WAL receiver, and applied WAL belongs to the startup process. He also did not want to change the check that returns NULL when no WAL receiver is ready, on security grounds. He suggested a separate view over XLogCtl, such as pg_stat_recovery, and returned the patch at the end of the CF.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
pg_stat_wal_receiver is just a one-one mapping with the shared memory
state of the WAL receiver itself and show data *if and only if* a WAL
receiver is running and iff it is ready to display any data, so I'd
rather not change its nature and it has nothing to do with the state
of WAL being applied by the startup process.  So this gets a -1 from
me.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical Decoding with timelines
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes logical decoding in the walsender follow timeline changes, as physical replication does, so that logical replication can cascade from a standby. It moved the walsender's send-pointer and timeline logic into shared functions used by both physical and logical sending.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Simon Riggs, the author, withdrew it as Returned with Feedback and said he had a new approach for the next release. Andres Freund noted that it covers only the walsender, while logical decoding also runs through SQL functions. He also said it does not let decoding start on a standby, which also needs forced hot_standby_feedback and slot cleanup in dbase_redo. Michael Paquier reported that the patch no longer applied, the earlier review comments were unaddressed, and no tests were shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Afaics the patch as is won't allow to start logical decoding on a standby.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add more TAP coverage for archive status with crash recovery of standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Add more TAP coverage for archive status with crash recovery of standbys
Reverted commit(s): Remove some unstable parts from new TAP test for archive status check
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This part of the test was included originally in 4e87c48, but got
reverted as of f9c1b8d because of timing issues in the test, where,
after more analysis, we found that the standbys may not have recovered
from the archives all the segments needed by the test.  This stabilizes
the test by making sure that standbys replay up to the position returned
by pg_switch_wal(), meaning that all segments are recovered before the
manual checkpoint that tests WAL segment recycling and its interactions
with archive status files.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid Copying WAL Segments Before Divergence to Speed Up pg_rewind
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_rewind skip copying WAL segments that come before the segment holding the last common checkpoint, since source and target share them. The author reported that WAL files are over 95% of the data pg_rewind copies in their setups.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not answer Michael Paquier's review of 2022-10-06, so the entry was marked returned with feedback. That review asked for tests that use command_checks_all() instead of reading log files, and an assertion that the WAL segment exists on both sides. It also asked about segments with older timelines and for WAL segments to be tracked in file_entry_t. Alexander Korotkov saw no design objections in the thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This review has been done a few weeks ago, and there has been no
update since, so I am marking this entry as returned with feedback in
the CF app.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow providing restore_command as a command line option to pg_rewind
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a -C/--target-restore-command option to pg_rewind, so that --restore-target-wal can fetch missing WAL when restore_command is not in $PGDATA/postgresql.conf. The command line option overrides any restore_command found in the configuration.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier closed the entry after commit 0d5c3875. He said that commit lets pg_rewind handle a postgresql.conf outside PGDATA through --config-file, which covers the case of this thread. He also objected to passing one command line as an option value of another command, because of quoting problems.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
FWIW, I am not much a fan of the design
where we pass down a command line as an option value of a different
command line (more games with quoting comes into mind first), and
--config-file should give enough room for the case of this thread.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fallback table AM for relkinds without storage
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a fallback table AM whose callbacks all raise an error, and assign it to relkinds without storage (views, foreign tables, partitioned tables) so that rd_tableam is never NULL. A wrong call into the table AM API for such a relation would then raise an error instead of crashing the backend.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund objected that the patch moves relkind-specific logic, such as choosing the slot type, into an AM that should never be called. He suggested separate AMs instead, for example one for foreign tables and one for sequences. Michael Paquier agreed he was not comfortable passing relkind knowledge into the AM, and he returned the entry because he was not sure what the right design was.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This doesn't seem like an advantage to me. Isn't this just pushing logic
away from a fairly obvious point into an AM that one would expect to
never actually get called?

precedents_retrieved.title: Use AF_UNIX for tests on Windows (ie drop fallback TCP code)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Thomas Munro proposed using AF_UNIX sockets for pg_regress and TAP tests on Windows too, removing the Windows-only TCP and SSPI setup code in the test harness. To match Unix security, mkdtemp() on Windows would create the socket directory with access for the current user only.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that with TCP gone from the Windows tests, the TCP socket code would have little test coverage on any platform, and reviewers asked for a switch that runs the tests over either TCP or Unix sockets. The author agreed, set the TAP test patch aside for more work and posted only the first two patches. Those later stopped applying, the author posted no new version, and the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If we remove that, won't we have a whole lot of code that's not
tested at all on any platform, ie all the TCP-socket code?

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert refactoring of restore command code to shell_restore.c
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert refactoring of restore command code to shell_restore.c
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 24c35ec and 57169ad.  PreRestoreCommand() and
PostRestoreCommand() need to be put closer to the system() call calling
a restore_command, as they enable in_restore_command for the startup
process which would in turn trigger an immediate proc_exit() in the
SIGTERM handler.  Perhaps we could get rid of this behavior entirely,
but 24c35ec has made the window where the flag is enabled much larger
than it was, and any Postgres-like actions (palloc, etc.) taken by code
paths while the flag is enabled could lead to more severe issues in the
shutdown processing.

Note that curculio has showed that there are much more problems in this
area, unrelated to this change, actually, hence the issues related to
that had better be addressed first.  Keeping the code of HEAD in line
with the stable branches should make that a bit easier.

Per discussion with Andres Freund and Nathan Bossart.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent matches: [P1] archives history files and [P2] renames .partial segments, and neither recorded reason applies to this proposal. Messages #2 and #5 point to a 2022 thread with an equivalent patch, which message #5 says this patch follows, but the material does not say why that thread ended without a commit.
The proposal adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or pg_dump state. The only compatibility issue from this angle is the behaviour change in back branches.
The core change keeps recovery off divergent WAL and adds no on-disk, catalog or protocol state. The only concern from this angle is how the behaviour change reaches back branches.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It changes which archived WAL file the startup process reads during recovery, and only superusers or the operator control that through restore_command, the archive and the timeline history; no new role, function, view or setting is involved. The new DEBUG1 message appears only at a debug log level and reveals no data beyond segment names.

The fix belongs in core and adds no hot-path cost, so the angle finds no fit problem. No committer has engaged in the visible thread yet. That limits committability, but it is no objection to the design.

This is a bug fix in XLogFileReadAnyTLI(). No existing setting, view or extension stops archive recovery from reading the parent timeline's copy of a switch-point segment, and an external tool cannot change which file recovery opens. The fix narrows the existing loop and adds no second mechanism.

The demand is real. This is a bugfix for silent replay of divergent WAL, seen in a production HA switchover (message #1). Ants Aasma reported the same bug in an earlier thread (message #2), and a reviewer reproduced it back to v12 (message #5). The cost falls on recovery only at segments it cannot find, and the thread weighed the changed stall behaviour (messages #1, #5).
